NextEra Energy, Inc. is an American energy company that is the world's largest electric utility holding company by market capitalization, with a valuation of over $187 billion as of July 2026.[5] NextEra Energy had revenues of $24.8 billion and 16,700 employees throughout the US and Canada in 2024.[6][7] It has a current generating capacity of 73 gigawatts.[8] Its subsidiaries include Florida Power & Light (FPL), NextEra Energy Resources (NEER), XPLR Energy Partners, and NextEra Energy Services.
FPL, the largest of its subsidiaries, is the third largest electric utility company in the United States.[9] NEER, together with its affiliated entities, is the world's largest generator of renewable energy from wind and solar.[10] In addition to wind and solar, NextEra Energy Resources owns and operates generating plants powered by natural gas, nuclear energy, and oil.[9] As of March 2025, approximately 36% of NextEra Energy's generating capacity was from fossil fuels and non-renewables, down from 41% in 2020. [7][8]
See also: Florida Power & Light § History
NextEra Energy traces its origins to 1925 with the formation of Florida Power & Light and the formation of FPL Group in 1984.[11][12]
The company purchased Colonial Penn in 1985[13] and sold it in 1991.[14] In 1998, FPL Group created FPL Energy, a subsidiary to manage FPL Group efforts outside of FPL's service area.[13] The same year, the company moved to acquire 37 power stations in Maine, Massachusetts, and New Jersey.[15] After a federal ruling would have limited the company's access to the New England power grid, FPL Group attempted to break off its purchase agreement in Maine,[16] but ultimately completed the purchase in March 1999.[17]
Through the early 2000s, FPL Group was the subject of multiple merger discussions, including with Iberdrola,[18][19] Entergy,[20] and Constellation Energy.[21] In 2005, FPL Group acquired Gexa Energy.[13]
In 2007, Florida's Public Service Commission rejected a plan by NextEra Energy to build a coal-burning power plant on 5,000 acres (20 km2) in Moore Haven, Florida, near the Everglades National Park. The National Park Service raised concerns that the coal plant would contaminate Lake Okeechobee with mercury and harm the Everglades.[22][23]
In 2008 the Environmental Protection Agency recognized FPL Group for achieving its goal to reduce its emissions by 21 percent per kilowatt hour.[24] The FPL Group Foundation, the company's philanthropic arm, donated $1 million to the Salvation Army in 2009 to help customers pay their power bills.[25] The following year, FPL Group rebranded as NextEra Energy. At the time, it provided electricity in 28 U.S. states and Canada.[13]
The 2010s saw additional merger and acquisition attempts by NEE, including with Hawaiian Electric Industries, Oncor Electric Delivery, SCANA, Santee Cooper, and Gulf Power Company.[26][27][28] Of these, only the Gulf Power acquisition was successful. The acquisition was completed in January 2019 and NEE merged Gulf Power with FPL in January 2022.[29][30] As part of the deal, NEE also acquired Plant Oleander and a 65 percent stake in the Stanton Energy Center natural gas power plants.[31] In July 2013, NextEra Energy partnered with Spectra Energy in a $3 billion investment for the construction of a natural gas pipeline in Florida.[32]
